alex: Heads-up: after rolling kernel 6.4 candidate in eu-west yesterday, we're seeing ~12% of P4/A100 hosts fail to bring up nvidia modules. Instances evicting GPU workloads.
maria: :eyes: what symptoms? logs?
alex: dmesg shows module verification failed / signature mismatch, then deferred probe. sample:
```
kernel: nvidia: disagrees about version of symbol module_layout
kernel: nvidia: version magic '6.4.0 SMP ...' should be '6.3.x'
kernel: nvidia: Unknown symbol nv_pci_init
nvidia_probe: driver registration failed -19
```
raj: Are these DKMS-built drivers or packaged vendor drivers?
alex: These are our image with CUDA 12.3 + nvidia-driver 535 installed via package (not DKMS). The hosts were reprovisioned yesterday with new kernel ABI. Looks like driver was built for previous kernel.
sam: Did the node pool autoscaler cause a mixture of kernels? any staging vs stable mismatch?
lena: eu-west kernel live patch job started at 02:12 UTC, autoscaler reprovisioned some older images; some nodes still on 6.3, some on 6.4 — mixed kernel pool.
maria: That would explain module verif mismatch. Any tainting/ooms?
alex: Yes, tainted hosts later OOM'd when CUDA drivers tried to initialize, causing NCCL handshake timeouts for training jobs. I'm seeing increased provisioning backoff.
ops-bot: [alert] 12 hosts in eu-west returned status: GPU_UNAVAILABLE between 02:15-03:05 UTC.
raj: Quick mitigation: drain affected nodes and fall back to kernel 6.3 images. Also mount host fallback: enable `module.sig_enforce=0`? risky.
sam: We should avoid kernel flags that disable verification in prod. Prefer node rollback to known-good driver + kernel pair.
lena: I'll hold further kernel rollouts and coordinate image rebuild with driver 535 compiled against 6.4 kernels.
maria: Can we hotfix by installing DKMS-built driver on reprovisioned nodes? That would rebuild against current kernel on boot.
alex: Try rolling a small canary with DKMS driver on 3 nodes. If green, propagate.
raj: Commands to test on a repro node:
```
sudo apt-get install -y nvidia-dkms-535
sudo dkms status
sudo reboot
# after reboot
nvidia-smi
dmesg | grep -i nvidia
```
sam: Also watch NCCL logs; if that looks healthy, remove autoscaler drain holds.
alex: I'll start canary now. tagging @oncall
oncall: acknowledged, monitoring.
ops-bot: [update] Canary nodes passed GPU initialization at 02:42 UTC. 3/3 OK.
maria: Great. Next steps: automate driver rebuild in image pipeline, add kernel-driver compatibility gate in rollouts, and add regression alert for "module verification" patterns.
lena: Opening a follow-up doc/PR for image pipeline. I'll add test matrix: kernels 5.15/6.3/6.4 + drivers 535/540.
alex: Thanks all. I'll keep this thread updated if we see new evicts.
alex: note: provisioning retries increased GPU bill by ~7% for eu-west during incident.
